IMPERIALISM — THEORETICAL LANDSCAPE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  THE PHENOMENON:
  Formal or informal political/economic control by a
  stronger state over a weaker one

  THEORETICAL SCHOOLS:
  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐
  │  ECONOMIC        │  │  POLITICAL /     │  │  CULTURAL /      │
  │  THEORIES        │  │  STRATEGIC       │  │  CIVILIZATIONAL  │
  │                  │  │  THEORIES        │  │  THEORIES        │
  │ Hobson: excess   │  │ Robinson-        │  │ Said: Orientalism│
  │  capital exports │  │  Gallagher:      │  │  — knowledge/    │
  │  demand colonies │  │  informal empire │  │  power nexus     │
  │                  │  │  preferable      │  │                  │
  │ Lenin: monopoly  │  │                  │  │ Civilizing       │
  │  capital, final  │  │ Schumpeter:      │  │  mission: moral  │
  │  stage of        │  │  atavistic       │  │  justification   │
  │  capitalism      │  │  warrior class   │  │  for control     │
  └──────────────────┘  └──────────────────┘  └──────────────────┘
         │                     │                     │
         └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘
                               ▼
                    CASE STUDIES:
                    British Empire · Scramble for Africa
                    French Empire · American informal empire
                    Post-colonial dependency theory
                    Chinese BRI (contemporary)

HOBSON'S MECHANISM:
  Income inequality at home
          │
          ▼
  Workers underpaid → underconsumption
          │
          ▼
  Capitalists have surplus capital with no profitable domestic use
          │
          ▼
  Capital exports to periphery seeking higher returns
          │
          ▼
  Political control (empire) needed to secure investment
          │
          ▼
  Imperial policy = finance capital's foreign policy

blocks.heading_context: ### Lenin: Imperialism as the Highest Stage
blocks.text:
LENIN'S FIVE FEATURES OF IMPERIALISM:
  1. Concentration → monopolies dominate economic life
  2. Bank + industrial capital merge → finance capital
  3. Capital export (not just goods) becomes decisive
  4. International monopoly combines divide the world
  5. Territorial division of the globe among great powers

ROBINSON-GALLAGHER SPECTRUM:
  Preference: ←─────────────────────────────────────────→
              Informal control          Formal annexation

  When informal works: Buenos Aires (British trade, no colony)
  When informal breaks down: Egypt 1882 (Arabi revolt → invasion)

  The decisive variable: local collaboration
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Empire works when there are reliable local allies    │
  │ (comprador class, collaborating elite)               │
  │                                                      │
  │ When the local collaborative structure collapses,    │
  │ Britain must either formalize control or withdraw    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

TWO TYPES OF COLONIAL STRUCTURE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  SETTLER COLONIALISM          EXTRACTION COLONIALISM
  ┌───────────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────────┐
  │ Goal: replace          │    │ Goal: extract        │
  │ indigenous population  │    │ resources/labor      │
  │                        │    │                      │
  │ Key mechanism:         │    │ Key mechanism:       │
  │ land seizure,          │    │ coerced labor,       │
  │ indigenous removal     │    │ plantation/mine      │
  │                        │    │ systems              │
  │ Examples: North        │    │ Examples: Belgian    │
  │ America, Australia,    │    │ Congo, British India │
  │ South Africa (Boer     │    │ (textile extraction),  │
  │ settler component),    │    │ Dutch East Indies    │
  │ Algeria (colons)       │    │                      │
  │                        │    │                      │
  │ Decolonization harder: │    │ Formal decolonization  │
  │ settler population     │    │ easier — no permanent  │
  │ remains                │    │ settler class to     │
  │ (Rhodesia, S. Africa,  │    │ displace             │
  │  Algeria)              │    │                      │
  └───────────────────────┘    └───────────────────────┘

BRITISH EMPIRE TIMELINE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  COMPANY ERA (1600-1858)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ East India Company as governing body for South Asia      │
  │ Mercantilist trading empire in Atlantic and Indian Ocean │
  │ Slave trade (abolished 1807), plantation economies       │
  │ Loss of American colonies (1776-83)                      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
  CROWN ERA / HIGH IMPERIALISM (1858-1914)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Crown rule in India (1858 — after Indian Rebellion)      │
  │ Free trade imperialism: global market integration        │
  │ Gold standard anchored by City of London                 │
  │ Scramble for Africa (1880s-1900s)                        │
  │ Peak: ~25% of world's land surface, ~23% of population   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
  IMPERIAL OVERSTRETCH (1914-1945)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ WWI: Empire mobilized (Indian Army, ANZAC, etc.)         │
  │ 1931: Statute of Westminster — Dominion autonomy         │
  │ Interwar: nationalist movements emerge everywhere        │
  │ WWII: fall of Singapore (1942) shatters invulnerability myth │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
  MANAGED WITHDRAWAL (1945-1975)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ India/Pakistan 1947, Burma/Ceylon 1948                   │
  │ African decolonization (Gold Coast 1957 → Rhodesia 1980)│
  │ "Wind of Change" speech (Macmillan, Cape Town, 1960)     │
  │ Last formal colonies (Hong Kong 1997, Falklands ongoing) │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
  INFORMAL EMPIRE / COMMONWEALTH
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Financial ties (Sterling Area), military bases           │
  │ Anglophone culture, BBC, common law systems              │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

SCRAMBLE FOR AFRICA — CAUSES DEBATE:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ METROPOLITAN CAUSATION:                              │
  │ Industrial capitalism seeking markets/materials      │
  │ (Hobson/Lenin model)                                 │
  │ → Problem: Africa was marginal in European trade     │
  │                                                      │
  │ STRATEGIC COMPETITION:                               │
  │ States scramble to deny rivals, not for positive gain│
  │ France vs. Britain vs. Germany zero-sum logic        │
  │                                                      │
  │ PERIPHERAL CAUSATION (Robinson-Gallagher):           │
  │ Egyptian financial crisis → British occupation →     │
  │ French feel excluded → scramble cascades             │
  │                                                      │
  │ TECHNOLOGICAL ENABLEMENT:                            │
  │ Quinine (malaria prophylaxis), Maxim gun, steamship  │
  │ lowered cost of African conquest dramatically        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

WHY EMPIRES END — STRUCTURAL FACTORS:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1. METROPOLITAN FISCAL COST                         │
  │    Maintaining empire becomes unprofitable          │
  │    (insurgency cost > extraction value)             │
  │                                                     │
  │ 2. PERIPHERAL NATIONALISM                           │
  │    Educated colonial elites use European political  │
  │    concepts (self-determination, democracy) against │
  │    the colonial power                               │
  │                                                     │
  │ 3. INTERNATIONAL NORMS SHIFT                        │
  │    Post-1945: UN Charter, self-determination,       │
  │    US anti-colonialism (at least in rhetoric)       │
  │    → Legitimacy of empire collapses globally        │
  │                                                     │
  │ 4. WWII DEMONSTRATION EFFECT                        │
  │    Colonial powers humiliated (France fell 1940,    │
  │    Singapore fell 1942) — myth of European          │
  │    superiority shattered                            │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

DEPENDENCY THEORY WORLD STRUCTURE:
  CORE                  SEMI-PERIPHERY           PERIPHERY
  (US, Europe, Japan)   (Brazil, Korea,           (sub-Saharan Africa,
                         Mexico)                   Central America)
        │                     │                       │
        ▼                     ▼                       ▼
  High-tech,            Mid-tech,                 Raw materials,
  capital goods,        some industry,            cheap labor,
  finance               exporting to core         exporting to all

  Terms of trade: manufactured goods rise in value faster
                  than commodities = structural disadvantage

blocks.heading_context: ## Chinese BRI as New Imperial Form?
blocks.text:
BRI — IMPERIAL OR NOT?
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  ARGUMENT FOR "IMPERIAL":         ARGUMENT AGAINST:
  ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────┐
  │ • "Debt trap" — loans    │    │ • Debt trap thesis weak  │
  │   create leverage        │    │   empirically (Deborah   │
  │   (Hambantota Port, SL)  │    │   Brautigam's critique)  │
  │                          │    │                          │
  │ • Chinese workers, not   │    │ • Host states have       │
  │   local employment       │    │   agency — negotiate     │
  │                          │    │                          │
  │ • Technology export      │    │ • South-South frame:     │
  │   creates surveillance   │    │   developing world       │
  │   infrastructure         │    │   solidarity, not        │
  │                          │    │   extraction             │
  │ • Conditions on          │    │                          │
  │   governance (media,     │    │ • No formal territorial  │
  │   politics)              │    │   control sought         │
  └──────────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────────┘

  VERDICT: BRI is better understood as mercantilist great power
  competition for influence than classical imperialism,
  but has structural effects that create dependency.
